title: Capacity Litmus Suite and Customer Certification Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Deliver a reproducible load-testing harness (Capacity Litmus Suite), a clear benchmarking methodology, and a customer-facing certification playbook that together define how we measure, validate, and certify Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior.

Scope:
- A portable load prober that can: run canary, ramp, sustain, and microburst profiles; inject multi-tenant mixes and realistic prompt length distributions; collect per-tenant and per-model tail latency (p50/p95/p99) and effective throughput.
- A benchmarking methodology document that formalizes measurement invariants, success criteria, statistical analysis (confidence intervals), and how to map results to SLOs and SLAs.
- A customer acceptance playbook (runbook + checklist) that support onboarding signoffs: expected inputs from customer, test configs, required telemetry dashboards, and signoff criteria.

Goals:
- Reduce ambiguity between internal throughput runs and customer acceptance results.
- Provide tooling that customers (or SEs) can run in dedicated environments or that we can run as part of Dedicated onboarding.
- Validate autoscaling policies (burst vs sustained), graceful degradation, and fallback routing under capacity pressure.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term UI for results in Console (separate project), embedded billing reconciliation (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A portable load harness (python + k6 wrapper) is committed to github with README and 3 canonical profiles: canary-ramp, steady-sustain, microburst
Benchmark methodology doc published to Confluence with measurement invariants, statistical analysis, and mapping to SLAs
Customer certification playbook drafted and includes a checklist, expected telemetry widgets, and a signoff template
Automated measurement artifacts (raw traces, token-level latency histograms, KV cache hit rates) are generated and stored in S3 for each run
Autoscaling policy validation tests that simulate burst and sustained load produce deterministic behavior within accepted variance thresholds (<=10% throughput variance at 95% confidence)
updates: 2026-02-20 - Created ticket: initial scope and stakeholders (SE onboarding, runtime, QA).

2026-02-24 - Spike completed: evaluated k6 + locust + custom grpc-prober. Chosen approach: python orchestrator + k6 for HTTP fanout + lightweight prober for websocket/streaming. Rationale: k6 provides efficient ramping and scripting; python orchestrator enables tenant mix and KV-caching instrumentation.

2026-03-02 - Draft harness prototype pushed to github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-litmus (internal). Initial profiles: canary-ramp and steady-sustain. Default workload uses 8 prompt length buckets derived from production token histogram.

2026-03-05 - Design review with Runtime team: decided to record per-token latency and KV cache hit ratios. Trade-off: collecting token-level telemetry increases storage cost but enables regression detection. Agreed to compress and sample traces. Follow-up: define sampling policy in benchmarking doc.

2026-03-08 - QA ran 10 sample runs against staging Dedicated pool. Findings: autoscaler cooldown of 90s causes transient tail latency spikes during microbursts. Action: add autoscaler tuning experiment to test matrix and include recommended policy adjustments in playbook.

2026-03-11 - Security/Privacy check: no customer PII included in default payloads. For customer runs, require cust-provided prompt redaction and KMS envelope guidelines. Added to playbook prerequisites.

2026-03-12 - Draft benchmarking methodology published to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Dedicated/Throughput+Litmus+Methodology. Next: stakeholder review (PM, Solutions Eng, Runtime).
notes: Integration note: the harness supports both hosted API endpoints and the Dedicated VPC ingress endpoint; tests add a header to indicate test traffic for easier telemetry filtering.

Customer acceptance flow: Solutions Eng runs initial baseline; if baseline passes, schedule joint run with customer (1h) using their realistic prompt set; collect artifacts and run automated signoff script.
Rollout plan: start with pilot customers (2 customers) in March; iterate on playbook based on pilot feedback; aim for GA documentation and tooling by end of Q2 2026.
